question_en:
I am preparing a biology lesson on "How repeating subunits assemble into hierarchical ring-shaped complexes." The attachment is a molecular structure teaching illustration saved previously, but the source was not recorded. Please answer the following questions based on the image:

1. **What is the official popular science series to which this image belongs?** Please provide the series name and the link to its archive-by-date page.
2. **Which official entries were published in this series in 2014?** Based on the archive-by-date page, cover January to December, and list the titles of all official entries by month. **Among the above entries, which entries have a main image that matches all the following characteristics?** In the same assembly, morphologically similar subunits are arranged repeatedly around a common center, forming a closed radial wheel; the center of the wheel has a clear opening; the ends of the outer spokes appear as paired blade-like modules. Please provide the titles of the entries that meet the criteria.

   When selecting images, uniformly use the first main image displayed after the title and one-sentence introduction of each detail page. If the main image depicts both free monomers and the complete assembly, judge only the complete assembly; do not use subsequent illustrations, images from "Exploring the Structure," or interactive views.

   Response format: For Question 1, provide the series name and the link to the archive-by-date page in text; for Question 2, use a table to list the month, title, and whether the main image meets the criteria for all official entries in 2014 by month.
answer:
Question 1: Series: RCSB PDB / PDB-101 — Molecule of the Month; Archive-by-date page: https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/motm-by-date

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 8-1-D01-1

## Step 01 · Trace the popular science series from the teaching illustration

Action: Perform an image search using clues from the molecular coloring, outline, and membrane schematic in the image. Example query: RCSB PDB Molecule of the Month HIV envelope glycoprotein illustration.

Evidence observation: The input corresponds to the main image of the January 2014 entry "HIV Envelope Glycoprotein." The series and author attribution on the detail page point to RCSB PDB/PDB-101's Molecule of the Month; this locating image is not the final visual hit.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/169
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/169/169-HIVEnvelopeGlycoprotein_4nco_composite.jpg
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/motm-image-download

Result of this step: Enter the archive-by-date page via the series.

## Step 02 · Extract the full year 2014 from the archive page

Action: Expand 2014 and record the official entries and detail links for each month from January to December; do not use keyword search results as a substitute for the complete annual list.

Evidence observation: There are 12 entries in 2014, with entry numbers 169 to 180 saved; the numbers only help associate pages, while months and titles are based on the archive text.

| Month | Title | Entry Number |
| --- | --- | --- |
| January 2014 | HIV Envelope Glycoprotein | 169 |
| February 2014 | Broadly Neutralizing Antibodies | 170 |
| March 2014 | Neurotransmitter Transporters | 171 |
| April 2014 | RecA and Rad51 | 172 |
| May 2014 | Aquaporin | 173 |
| June 2014 | GFP-like Proteins | 174 |
| July 2014 | Microtubules | 175 |
| August 2014 | Dynein | 176 |
| September 2014 | Apoptosomes | 177 |
| October 2014 | Ebola Virus Proteins | 178 |
| November 2014 | Methyl-coenzyme M Reductase | 179 |
| December 2014 | TAL Effectors | 180 |

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/motm-by-date

Result of this step: All 12 entries proceed to main image inspection.

## Step 03 · Determine the uniform main image and spatial criteria

Action: Enter the first main image displayed after the title and one-sentence introduction of each entry; when both free monomers and the complete assembly appear, judge only the latter.

Evidence observation: Check sequentially: repeating similar subunits arranged around a common center forming a closed radial wheel; a clear opening at the center of the wheel; paired blade-like modules at the end of every outer spoke. Not all ring-shaped molecules or any structures with holes meet these criteria; subsequent illustrations and interactive views must not be used as substitutes.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/motm-by-date

Result of this step: Compare the assemblies in the 12 main images on the same scale.

## Step 04 · Check January 2014: HIV Envelope Glycoprotein

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: The main image is a side view of a compact trimer on a membrane, not a radial wheel. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/169
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/169/169-HIVEnvelopeGlycoprotein_4nco_composite.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 05 · Check February 2014: Broadly Neutralizing Antibodies

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Antibodies bind to a compact envelope complex; there is no wheel-like repeating assembly. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/170
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/170/170-BroadlyNeutralizingAntibodies_4nco_bnAb.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 06 · Check March 2014: Neurotransmitter Transporters

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Side view of a single membrane transporter; no repeating radial spokes are visible. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/171
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/171/171-NeurotransmitterTransporters_4m48.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 07 · Check April 2014: RecA and Rad51

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Proteins form an extended helical filament along DNA, not closing into a radial platform. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/172
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/172/172-RecAAndRad51_recA_filament.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 08 · Check May 2014: Aquaporin

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: The compact tetramer lacks outer spokes with paired blades at the ends. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/173
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/173/173-Aquaporin_1fqy.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 09 · Check June 2014: GFP-like Proteins

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Four compact fluorescent protein subunits are arranged in a block shape; there are no spokes or a central ring hole. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/174
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/174/174-GFPLikeProteins_1g7k.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 10 · Check July 2014: Microtubules

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Tubulin forms an oblique cylindrical wall, not the required frontal radial wheel. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/175
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/175/175-Microtubules_3j2u.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 11 · Check August 2014: Dynein

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Although the dynein motor domain has a ring-like outline, it belongs to the domain arrangement of a single motor and lacks repeating outer spokes with paired blades. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/176
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/176/176-Dynein_3vkh-label.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 12 · Check September 2014: Apoptosomes

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: The complete assembly on the right consists of repeating blue subunits forming a closed radial wheel, with a clear central opening and paired blue blades at the end of each spoke; the free monomers on the left are not included in the judgment. Closed radial wheel = Yes; Center opening = Yes; Outer paired blades = Yes.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/177
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/177/177-Apoptosomes_human_apoptosome.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: Yes.

## Step 13 · Check October 2014: Ebola Virus Proteins

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: The main image is a longitudinal section of the virus structure; the interior is a solid helical core, not a radial platform with an open center. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/178
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/178/178-Ebola_Virus_Proteins-EbolaProteins2018.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 14 · Check November 2014: Methyl-coenzyme M Reductase

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: The enzyme is a compact globular assembly without radial spokes or a distinct central opening. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/179
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/179/179-MethylCoenzymeMReductase_1mro.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 15 · Check December 2014: TAL Effectors

Action: Confirm the main image position and sequentially check the three spatial features for the same assembly.

Evidence observation: Repeating domains are arranged helically along DNA and cannot form a closed radial wheel. Closed radial wheel = No; Center opening = No; Outer paired blades = No.

Evidence links:
https://pdb101.rcsb.org/motm/180
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/180/180-TALEffectors_3ugm.jpg

Result of this step: Main image meets all criteria: No.

## Step 16 · Review exclusion of similar ring-shaped structures

Action: Compare September's Apoptosomes with the easily confused August Dynein and July Microtubules.

Evidence observation: September features multiple repeating subunits jointly forming a wheel with paired blades; August has only a motor domain ring, and July is a cylindrical wall. One cannot include answers based solely on "having a ring or a hole."

Evidence links:
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/177/177-Apoptosomes_human_apoptosome.jpg
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/176/176-Dynein_3vkh-label.jpg
https://cdn.rcsb.org/pdb101/motm/175/175-Microtubules_3j2u.jpg

Result of this step: Only Apoptosomes is Yes; the other 11 entries are No.

## Step 17 · Verify output scope and format

Action: Fill in the current question prompt item by item with the full candidate set, the visual screening results, and the subsequent text conditions.

Evidence observation: No missing months among the 12; the final response includes the series name and the archive-by-date page link, as well as a 12-row main image judgment table arranged by month.

Result of this step: Output the answer as required by the question; keep the search explanation and exclusion reasons in the trajectory.
